label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 11
knowledgePattern: Negate a supplied three-level quantified definition
solution:
The supplied property has the order ∀h>0∃d>0∀x∈R. Negating swaps each quantifier but preserves its position and domain: ∃h>0∀d>0∃x∈R.

The innermost statement is an implication: |x−a|<d implies |f(x)−f(a)|<h. It fails when the premise holds and the conclusion fails, giving |x−a|<d and |f(x)−f(a)|≥h.

Together, the negation says that there is a positive h such that, for every positive d, some real x satisfies both of those inequalities. This is option C. The same fixed h works against every d; x may depend on d.

hints.title: Negate from the outside inward
hints.body: Write the order of the three quantified choices before changing any inequalities. Swap each universal and existential quantifier, leaving its domain and position unchanged.
hints.recap: Negate the whole claim from the outer quantifier inward, preserving the order and allowed inputs.
hints.pitfall: Reordering the quantifiers changes the claim.
hints.pause: Write the new quantifier order and decide which later choices may depend on earlier ones.

recall.reminder: Negate the whole claim from the outer quantifier inward, preserving the order and allowed inputs.

hints.title: Negate the conditional part
hints.body: Name the near-input condition P and the near-output condition Q. Work out exactly when the implication from P to Q fails.
hints.recap: An implication is false precisely when its premise is true and its conclusion is false.
hints.pitfall: Negating a strict inequality includes equality in its complement.
hints.pause: Combine this condition with your quantifiers and compare the entire statement with each option.
